issue.standard_remedy: Qualify a second source and shift volume
issue.summary: High-risk supplier (score 53.1) holds 17% of a category

plan.diagnosis: Eagle Pacific Chemicals represents a concentrated medium-severity risk with 16.9% share of its category and USD 505,804 in annual spend. The supplier's risk score of 53.1 is driven by poor resiliency (score 32), weak ESG performance (score 39), and failure class 4, creating supply continuity and reputational exposure for the organization.

remedy_steps.step: Launch RFI to identify and pre-qualify 2-3 alternative suppliers in the same chemical category with risk scores below 40 and resiliency scores above 50
Negotiate trial orders (10-15% of current volume, approximately USD 50,000-75,000) with the highest-ranked alternative supplier to validate quality and delivery performance
Implement dual-source strategy targeting 60/40 split between Eagle Pacific Chemicals and qualified second source, reducing Eagle Pacific's category share from 16.9% to approximately 10%
Engage Eagle Pacific Chemicals on ESG improvement roadmap with quarterly scorecards; tie 5% of volume retention to achieving ESG score of 50+ within 12 months
Establish safety stock buffer of 30 days for critical SKUs from Eagle Pacific (estimated USD 40,000 inventory investment) until second source is fully ramped

plan.expected_impact: Reduce concentrated risk exposure by USD 175,000-200,000 (35-40% of current spend) through dual-sourcing, lowering category concentration from 16.9% to ~10% and mitigating supply disruption risk from a failure class 4 supplier.
kpis: Eagle Pacific category share reduced to ≤10% within 90 days
Second source qualified and handling 30-40% of volume (USD 150,000-200,000 annually) by day 90
Eagle Pacific ESG score improvement to ≥45 within 6 months, ≥50 within 12 months
Zero supply disruptions from Eagle Pacific during transition period
Weighted average supplier risk score for category reduced from 53.1 to ≤45
risks: Quality variation or delivery failures from new second source during ramp-up period
Eagle Pacific may reject volume reduction, leading to price increases or relationship deterioration on remaining 60% of business
Transition costs (re-qualification, tooling, inventory buffer) estimated at USD 50,000-75,000
Cross-ERP complexity: chemical purchases may span SAP, Oracle EBS, and Coupa, requiring synchronized vendor master and sourcing rule changes
Failure class 4 indicator suggests elevated bankruptcy or operational failure risk during 90-day transition window
erp_actions: SAP: Create new vendor master records (XK01) for qualified alternative suppliers with appropriate purchase organization assignments and payment terms (net 45)
SAP: Add source list entries (ME01) for alternative supplier across affected material numbers with quota arrangement 60% Eagle Pacific / 40% new source effective day 90
Oracle EBS: Update supplier site assignments and create new approved supplier list (ASL) entries for alternative vendor in chemicals category
Coupa: Add new supplier to preferred supplier list with catalog enablement; configure requisition routing rules to enforce dual-source split
SAP: Implement purchase order release strategy with additional approval step (over USD 25,000) for Eagle Pacific orders during transition period (ME28)
All ERPs: Update vendor master payment terms from net 30 to net 45 for Eagle Pacific to improve cash flow leverage during volume reduction
SAP: Add vendor master memo (LFA1) flagging Eagle Pacific risk score and dual-source requirement for all buyers
NetSuite/Dynamics 365: If chemicals purchasing occurs in these systems, replicate source list and preferred vendor configurations with same quota logic
